kept.title: Note-node IDs use a millisecond timestamp with NO random suffix — same-ms collision risk
kept.summary: addNoteNode mints id = `note-${Date.now().toString(36)}` (lib/overlay.js:180), with no randomness. addGhost right below uses Date.now()+Math.random(). Two notes created within the same millisecond (e.g. a batch inject loop) can collide on id and silently overwrite. This is a latent bug, not visible from the function name.

kept.title: Git ops target an arbitrary repo, NOT the daemon workspace — resolve repoPath > task.repo > workspace
kept.summary: Every git/measure/merge op resolves its repo by precedence explicit repoPath > the task's overlay `repos[key]` field > the daemon workspace, because the common case is the workspace is NOT itself a git repo. Worktrees+branches are keyed by sha1(repo path) so distinct repos never collide on disk. Forgetting set_task_repo silently runs git against the wrong tree.

kept.title: Winner merge auto-aborts on conflict and never forces — judge escalates instead
kept.summary: merge() uses `git merge --no-ff`; on conflict it collects conflicted paths via diff --diff-filter=U, then runs `git merge --abort` to leave a CLEAN tree and returns {merged:false, conflict:true, files}. It NEVER resolves or forces. Callers (the judge) must handle the conflict + escalate; assuming merge always lands is wrong.

kept.title: Native task JSON is read-only to us; all non-native state lives in the overlay
kept.summary: Native task files are the source of truth for native fields (status, intra-session deps) but are unsafe to write (.lock, may be overwritten by Claude Code) and are confined to lib/native-tasks.js. Everything else (cross-session/workspace edges, richer status, notes, summaries, per-task repo, metrics) lives in OUR per-workspace overlay store. Mutate native ONLY via TaskUpdate — never write the file.

kept.title: Cross-session task IDs MUST be namespaced session-uuid/id — bare ids are session-local
kept.summary: Native task IDs are local ('1','2',…) and unique only within one session dir. Any cross-session reference must be {session-uuid}/{id} (e.g. the task keys c0bd3682…/7). A bare id will resolve to the wrong task or none. Native sessions share no tasks (only Agent Teams share, within one team).

kept.title: search_knowledge / GET /search is lexical token-overlap, not embeddings
kept.summary: Retrieval scores each node by token overlap (suggestToks/scoreNodeAgainstTokens) of the query against label+summary, filters score>0, sorts desc, slices k (default 5, max 50). It is purely lexical: a note only retrieves if it shares surface tokens with the query — so note WORDING matters for recall. There is no semantic/embedding match.

kept.title: The stop signal has ONE source of truth shared by the hook and the in-process heartbeat
kept.summary: stopSignalFor(session) (daemon.js:261) is the single resolver for cancel_requested (per-task) and stop_requested (per-agent); it backs BOTH the /should-stop route (PreToolUse hook) and the heartbeat's decideAction. So a flagged stop halts an in-process loop the SAME way it halts a hooked CLI agent — don't add a second divergent stop check.

kept.title: Daemon stays mechanical; judgement/planning live in subagent skills
kept.summary: Deliberate split: the daemon only exposes isolated worktrees + a merge primitive + mechanical iterate-vs-stop control (lib/optimize.js, decided by rule precedence, NOT by an LLM free-choice). Judgement, planning, and benchmark research are subagent SKILLS. If a skill wants a new daemon endpoint to make a decision, it is probably overreaching — push the intelligence to the skill.

kept.title: A stuck optimization escalates to a human and HALTS — it never auto-cancels the problem
kept.summary: When the last K rounds yield no usable winner (all no-winner / all guardrail-regressed), the loop raises request_guidance and stops rather than quietly dropping or replanning. One of exactly five escalation triggers. So a genuinely-broken metric problem reaches a human instead of silently vanishing from the graph.

kept.title: Measure benchmark work by output_tokens, not a gross-minus-plumbing 'net'
kept.summary: MCP token attribution is sticky and buckets cache_read into 'plumbing', so a gross−plumbing 'net' produces a spurious '65% less work' artifact. Trust output_tokens for actual work and cost-weighted gross (cache_read ×0.1) for cost. This is the methodology that produced the v2–v5 NO-WIN readings — re-deriving 'net' will mislead you the same way.

kept.title: Context cost is ENTIRELY payload size; a lean payload reaches cost parity
kept.summary: A/B finding (v2→v3): work was parity ON vs OFF on self-solvable tasks; the whole ON-vs-OFF cost delta was cache_read from re-attending the loaded payload + tool schemas each turn. Shrinking get_learnings (~25k → ~1-3k via compact:true) brought cost to parity. No work/quality benefit was measured — unproven, not disproven. THIS is why the onboarding reframe scores COMPETENCE, not tokens.

kept.title: Desktop app runs .mcp.json servers but NOT settings.json hooks
kept.summary: So the MCP server self-boots the daemon and registers the workspace on startup — the graph + tools work hookless. Hook-only features (auto-router PreToolUse gate, terminal status line) require the CLI; in the desktop app the orchestration discipline is instruction-level only. Don't assume the gate hook is enforcing anything in the desktop app.
